sum: From Lukla and Namche up the Dudh Koshi to the lakes at Gokyo, with a climb of Gokyo Ri (5,357 m), a day walk to the fifth lake and a return through Phortse.

guide.note: Khumbu has not enforced the national guide requirement, so you can walk to Gokyo independently. A licensed guide is still worth the fee in this valley: the trail gains height faster than the base camp route, beds between Dole and Gokyo are limited, and someone who knows the early signs of altitude illness can turn you round before it becomes an evacuation.

access: The trek starts and ends at the Lukla airstrip. Morning flights go from Kathmandu or, in the busiest weeks of spring and autumn, from Manthali in Ramechhap. Cloud or wind cancels them often enough that a spare day belongs in every plan.

photo.a: A turquoise lake with a cluster of lodges on its shore lies beside the grey, rubble-covered Ngozumpa glacier, with snow peaks including Cholatse on the skyline.
photo.c: Gokyo lake and the Ngozumpa glacier from Gokyo Ri

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Sagarmatha park and Khumbu municipality permits
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
airport transfers; Kathmandu hotel nights in some packages

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.

transportText: Flights to Lukla and back, from Kathmandu or (in the busy months) from Manthali with a night drive to the airstrip
tips: Carry all the cash you need from Kathmandu or Namche; nothing above Namche dispenses money.
Dole and Machhermo have far fewer beds than villages on the base camp trail. In October and April arrive by early afternoon or have a guide phone ahead.
At Gokyo, ask your lodge about the state of the east-bank trail before you commit to the descent through Phortse.
Sunlight off the lakes and old snow is fierce. Wear proper sunglasses and sunscreen even on cold days.
Treat all drinking water and aim for three to four litres a day; the dry air takes more out of you than you notice.

days.t: Fly to Lukla, walk to Phakding
days.note: The flight is over by mid-morning. The trail drops through Chheplung to the Dudh Koshi and follows it to Phakding, so you finish the first afternoon 250 m lower than you started.

Several bridge crossings, a permit check at Monjo, then the 600 m hill from the last high bridge to Namche. Climb it at the pace of a loaded porter and you will arrive in better shape than those who hurried.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Walk up to the ridge at 3,880 m for a first sight of Everest and come back down to sleep. Tomorrow's stage gains 600 m in one go, so do the walk even if you feel fine.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Leave the base camp trail at Sanasa and climb to the chorten at Mong La, lose 300 m through forest to Phortse Tenga, then climb for two hours past waterfalls, frozen in the colder months, to Dole. The last hour is where the height starts to tell.
A short morning along open hillside through the yak pastures of Lhafarma and Luza, with Cho Oyu coming into view at the head of the valley. Walk slowly and be in Machhermo for lunch.

Stay a second night. In the morning climb the ridge north of the lodges for an hour or so, for a view up the valley to Cho Oyu and the end of the Ngozumpa Glacier, then rest. If the rescue post is staffed, go to its afternoon altitude talk.

Beyond Pangka the trail climbs a stone staircase beside the stream that drains the glacier, then levels out past the first and second lakes to Gokyo on the third. Not far, but at this height it takes longer than the distance suggests.

The path crosses the stream at the north end of the lake and zigzags 570 m up the hillside. Allow two to three hours up and one down. Go before dawn for clear air, or after lunch on a settled day for evening light on Everest.

An easy hour up the trough between moraine and hillside to the fourth lake, then a rougher stretch to the fifth. Climb the moraine crest beside it for the view of Cho Oyu and Everest. Take lunch and water, and turn back by midday if cloud is building.

days.t: Gokyo to Phortse by the east bank
days.note: Go back down past the lakes, cross the river below the glacier snout to Na and follow the east side of the valley through Thare, Thore and Konar. A long day of contouring with only a few basic tea houses. In snow or ice, descend through Machhermo and Dole instead.
Drop to the bridge at Phortse Tenga, climb 300 m back up to Mong La and follow the balcony trail to Namche. It is short enough to leave the afternoon free for a hot shower and the bakeries.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Down the Namche hill, along the rolling valley trail and up the final rise into Lukla. Go to the airline office when you arrive and reconfirm tomorrow's seat.
Flights to Kathmandu or Manthali start at first light when the weather allows. If Lukla is closed you wait for the next clear morning, share a helicopter or begin walking toward the road.
